Patient/proxy role: Often essential for adherence, last dose, self-ceased and OTC use
Potential conflicts: MedicationRequest active but patient stopped; dispense without ingestion
Default reconciliation principle: Triangulate; prescription/dispense do not prove current use
Freshness consideration: Very high: current/last dose often perioperatively time-critical

Patient/proxy role: Can report but is not authoritative for legal/current order details
Default reconciliation principle: Prescribing source defines order; retain actual-use statement separately
Auto-resolution?: Usually yes for order identity if source valid/current

Patient/proxy role: May add context but source system records administration event
Default reconciliation principle: Administration record preferred for documented administered dose; discrepancy retained if clinically relevant

Preferred/strong sources: Verified allergy record + specialist/testing + source documents
Patient/proxy role: Patient report is safety-significant even if unverified
Potential conflicts: Record says NKDA; patient reports anaphylaxis
Default reconciliation principle: Never suppress new patient-reported serious reaction because record lacks it; escalate/reconcile

Patient/proxy role: Often key source for symptoms experienced
Default reconciliation principle: Preserve patient description; retrieve record when severity/agent matters

Potential conflicts: Patient says difficult airway; prior chart unavailable or contradictory
Default reconciliation principle: Treat serious patient report as unresolved safety signal until corroborated/refuted, not as confirmed diagnosis

Preferred/strong sources: Patient is usually primary source; clinician assessment/objective data supplements
Potential conflicts: Old record denies symptom; patient now reports it
Default reconciliation principle: Current patient report outranks stale absence for current symptom; objective data may modify interpretation

Preferred/strong sources: Clinician-authored records, specialist letters, diagnostic results
Patient/proxy role: Can accurately report known diagnoses and may reveal missing record data
Potential conflicts: Patient label differs from formal diagnosis
Default reconciliation principle: Preserve both; verify when distinction affects perioperative management

Patient/proxy role: Patient may report approximate result but not substitute for source when exact value matters
Default reconciliation principle: Lab source preferred for value; patient statement retained as separate assertion

Patient/proxy role: Patient may provide home values separately
Default reconciliation principle: Do not overwrite; represent source/context separately

Potential conflicts: Old record conflicts with current report
Default reconciliation principle: Current patient report generally preferred for current behaviour; preserve temporal change

Preferred/strong sources: Patient narrative + validated instrument + observed performance where available
Default reconciliation principle: Current narrative/instrument dated separately; do not silently average

Potential conflicts: Conversation text must not create identity

Patient/proxy role: Patient understanding useful but not authoritative for exact planned procedure
Default reconciliation principle: Treat discrepancy as safety-critical workflow issue

Patient/proxy role: Patient can state current wishes; may supersede old understanding subject to legal/clinical process
Potential conflicts: Document and current expressed preference differ
Default reconciliation principle: Surface discrepancy to clinician; do not infer from document title
